findings.title: Backup code check and use is not atomic
findings.body: When logging in with a backup code, authorize() reads the decrypted `backupCodes` array, checks `indexOf(credentials.backupCode...)`, and then updates the user row with the consumed code set to null. These are separate non-transactional operations. Two concurrent requests using the same valid backup code can both pass the `index === -1` check before either update runs, so a one-time backup code can authenticate more than once. The code should be consumed atomically, e.g. via a transaction or a conditional update on the current encrypted value.

findings.title: Successful 2FA enable is not reported if dialog is closed by native close
findings.body: `handleEnable` now ends with `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` instead of calling `onEnable`. Only the explicit `backup-codes-close` button calls `onEnable` later. If the dialog is closed with its built-in close control, Escape, or overlay through the `onOpenChange` prop on line 166, the parent never receives `onEnable`, so the settings UI can remain out of sync with the server even though 2FA has already been enabled. Handle dialog close during the backup-codes step or call `onEnable` immediately on successful enable.

findings.title: Core backup-code login/disable paths are untested
findings.body: The PR adds backup-code login and backup-code disabling, but the only added e2e assertions cover showing the backup codes during setup, the download filename, the copy toast, and closing the dialog. It does not test that a generated backup code can be used to complete login when 2FA is required, nor that it can be used to disable 2FA. The TODO at line 12 explicitly acknowledges this. Security-critical one-time-code behavior should have success and rejection e2e coverage.

findings.title: Clipboard write failure is reported as success
findings.body: The copy handler calls `navigator.clipboard.writeText(...)` without awaiting or catching its promise, and immediately calls `showToast(t("backup_codes_copied"), "success")`. Clipboard access can fail due to permissions or document focus, so users can be told the codes were copied when they were not, and an unhandled promise rejection can appear in the console. Await the write and only show success if it resolves.
